result: Stratifying ME/CFS by immune competence, immunodeficient patients had reduced complement C4a while non-immunodeficient patients had elevated LPS-binding protein (ELISA); no sample sizes or effect sizes given.
reason: Measures C4a in ME/CFS and adds an immune-competence subgroup, fitting the heterogeneous-complement claim; LBP part also bears on gut-translocation-lps.

result: In 277 long COVID clinic patients vs 50 controls, 15% had an abnormal NASA lean test (7% PoTS, 8% OH), 52% developed OI symptoms during the test, and 45% of abnormal tests had no prior OI symptoms.
reason: Same test in a long COVID population, but it does not measure the rising HR with narrow pulse pressure in recent-onset ME/CFS, so it extends rather than replicates.

result: On a standardised NASA lean test, 7% of 277 long COVID clinic patients met PoTS criteria (11% with a one-reading threshold) vs none of 50 controls, while 52% had OI symptoms during the test.
reason: Long COVID, not ME/CFS, prevalence estimate; shows low rate and protocol dependence, which extends the claim rather than replicating it in ME/CFS.

result: In 3,783 PRIME participants, questionnaire-assessed PEM was present in 48.1% of women and 41.2% of men with post-COVID condition (OR 4.38 and 4.78 vs never-positive) and OI in 29.3% and 27.9% (OR 3.06 and 2.71).
reason: Measures PEM and OI prevalence by questionnaire, not ME/CFS criteria or incidence, so it belongs with long COVID PEM prevalence.

result: In combined data from 219 ME/CFS patients, tilt-induced %CBF reduction was 25, 29 and 33% in mild, moderate and severe ICC disease; in 71 patients retested for worsening symptoms, severity rose but the mean CBF reduction was 24% at both visits.
reason: Same Doppler CBF-on-tilt measure, adding a severity gradient; van Campen 2023 is not among the cited studies. The retest arm showed no within-person change.

result: In 42 non-hospitalised PACS patients (with or without POTS) vs 21 controls, about 200 of 700 cardiometabolic proteins were dysregulated (>90% up), with hemostasis, immune, metabolic and angiogenesis pathways enriched, 11 of 33 cytokines raised, and no difference between POTS and non-POTS groups.
reason: Long COVID proteomic pathway enrichment, not routine coagulation markers in ME/CFS; no atlas finding measures this.

result: 88 post-COVID patients with cognitive complaints had longer reaction times than 50 matched controls (r = 0.51), a selective processing-speed deficit that persisted without improvement at 6-month follow-up (n=77).
reason: Same reaction-time and processing-speed measure in long COVID, adding a longitudinal course.

result: Systematic review of 17 resting qEEG studies: CFS/ME trended toward increased low-frequency (delta, theta, alpha) and reduced beta activity, the opposite of FMS, while long COVID findings were mixed.
reason: Already cited: this is the preprint of Silva-Passadouro 2024 (Clin Neurophysiol), which is in finding_studies.
